night2.measures: Per-man rows from memory (memreader, mem_extras: A, B, C and E bound) every 0.1 s while B and E are within 105 m before the contact, every 0.5 s after it - the behind plan's rows. A start: a living man present in two consecutive polls whose strike mark rose, given to the unit owning the man in his tgt at the later poll. In reach: a living enemy man within 4.0 m (centres). t: s from A's first melee flag (unit samples); tau: s from the joiner's own first melee flag ('two': the earlier of B's and C's - R4's oldest junior). A rate: starts over the span of the polls in the window. 'Over hold': over the mean of the same-width hold lanes (h24 / h30 / h36 / h30L, B never ordered) of the same pair's rate in the same seconds from their A flag. Mean +- one standard error over lanes; 'within two errors of N (+- e)': |m - N| <= 2 sqrt(se^2 + e^2). Code: tmp/probe_night2/ext.py, series.py, tlib.py, tables.py (tmp/sim_behind/lane_series.py's definitions: the numbers compare with behind's tab1 / chk_tables). Losses: game/probe/unit_probe.py behind2_measure (behind_measure's windows 30 / 60 / 120 / 240 s from the sample before the lane's first flag, + 480 on the long lanes).

decision.question: is a hammer that charges DEEP into a flank a class-K junior like the corner joiner (its take y(tau) x the senior's line; the anvil's relief x(tau) by the pooled table), or does the depth of the wrap give it more (men in reach growing with the wrap)?
decision.measure: deep_flank (4 lanes; shallow_flank 4 reported beside): tau from the hammer H's first melee flag; x(tau) = 1 - T>A / the same target's stand lanes' T>A over the same seconds from A's flag (A the anvil, T the clanrats); y(tau) = T>H / the same; H's men in reach of T (4 m) by bin; bins 5-15 / 15-30 / 30-45 / 45-105 s (0-5 s printed). Per-man rows as behind's (mem_extras: the anvil's men too).
decision.K: x within two errors of the table in at least 3 of the 4 bins and the mean over the 4 bins within 0.05 of the table's mean (0.194) -> the deep hammer is a K junior with the pooled table: S1 as built, no depth term
decision.more: x above the table by more than two errors in at least 2 bins AND H's men in reach rising from bin 5-15 to 45-105 by more than two errors -> the wrap gives more: K's relief needs a term by the junior's men in reach (or its depth along the flank); the table under-relieves a deep hammer
decision.less: x below the table by more than two errors in at least 2 bins -> a deep hammer relieves less than the corner joiner: K needs a cap by depth
decision.gap_0_60: the twin-vs-game gap seen on these lanes at 0-60 s (tmp/tactic_slice/review_attack_v23.md, check 11: shallow front twin 0.097 against game 0.026, shallow place 0.115 against 0.055 - the twin about threefold): read from the men's rows - H's men in reach of T, H>T, T>H, A>T, T>A starts a second at 0-20 / 20-60 s from H's flag in shallow_front / shallow_place against stand - which of who-is-in-reach and who-starts-swings carries it (no decision line: stated)

verdict.line: K FOR THE RELIEF, NOT FOR THE TAKE. deep_flank x at tau 5-15 / 15-30 / 30-45 / 45-105 s 0.065 +- 0.073 / 0.143 +- 0.032 / 0.198 +- 0.032 / 0.212 +- 0.023 against the table's 0.115 / 0.17 / 0.22 / 0.27: within two errors in 3 of 4 (45-105 below by 2.5 errors), mean 0.154 against 0.194 -> by the line 'K like the corner joiner'; the hammer's men in reach do NOT grow with the wrap (23.2 +- 1.6 -> 19.3 +- 0.1). shallow_flank the same verdict (0.097 / 0.148 / 0.166 / 0.269; reach 29.6 -> 16.7). But the hammer's take y = E>H over stand's E>A is 0.54 / 0.41 / 0.42 / 0.38 (deep) and 0.35 / 0.37 / 0.31 / 0.22 (shallow) against y's 0.19 / 0.21 / 0.26 / 0.285, and E's total is 1.48 / 1.27 / 1.23 / 1.17 (deep): a flank hammer ADDS blows - E's flank men turn and strike it (frames at A's flag + 35 s) - instead of taking them off the anvil. So K's relief table holds for a deep flank hammer, its take is its own flank line, not y x the senior's line: R6 (K takes y x line) is refuted for a flank hammer. The rear hammer gets no relief at all (x -0.11..+0.10, y 0.6-0.7, total 1.6-1.75); front / place hammers are corner joiners (x near the table or under it, y 0.12-0.23, total 0.92-1.12).
